items.text: Combining long-term hair with recent plasma in real-world PrEP services to study exposure/use patterns, effectiveness, and renal outcomes, making full use of existing cohorts.
Extending hair measurement to topical rings and cross-comparing with plasma, residual drug, and self-report to examine the incremental value of different biomarkers.

Studying individual PK of long-acting CAB and dosing interval changes; Aim 3 is a treatment cohort, and the resulting calibration can provide methods for future prevention studies rather than directly proving preventive effectiveness.

Hair concentration is simultaneously influenced by use, PK, and hair biology; observational exposure–infection relationships and drug use varying with risk do not automatically yield a causal protective threshold.

Drugs and routes of administration require independent validation; spiked hair does not equal reliable detection in real subjects; 0.25 cm ≈ one week, plasma-to-hair conversion, and local tissue protection all await calibration.

Effective event numbers and sparse subgroups constrain thresholds and predictive precision; the overlap of cases plus random non-case sampling and renal events must be handled according to the committed weights, and missing hair/refusals and incomplete visits may still introduce selection bias.
